# `m.forex.last_quote`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The latest best bid and ask of each currency pair.

```python
m.forex.last_quote(symbols)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Methods | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol`; `mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND` also keys by `Timestamp` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Currency pairs, such as `C:EURUSD`. `dm.ALL` is refused; use `m.forex.snapshots(dm.ALL)` instead. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST: the request's `from` parameter. | REST |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the UTC date of `Timestamp`. | REST |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `timestamp`: "The Unix millisecond timestamp." | REST |
| `BidPrice` | double | The bid price. | REST |
| `AskPrice` | double | The ask price. | REST |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/forex/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
